newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Ericsson, Nokia rise to 12-month highs.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Ericsson, Nokia rise to 12-month highs.

text.p: Nordic telecom equipment companies Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson and Nokia Group rose to a 12-month highs Wednesday to highlight trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Ericsson was up 1-1/4 to 39-1/2, above the 12-month high of 39-1/4, after Smith Barney analyst Tony Langham set an 18-month price target of $59 for the shares.
Ericsson was the most active ADR on the New York exchanges.
Nokia rose two to 76, also a 12-month high, after Langham set an 18-month price target of $114 for the shares. Smith Barney has a buy recommendation on both shares.
British drug stocks rose. Glaxo Wellcome Plc was up 13/16 to 42-7/8, above a 12-month closing high, and SmithKline Beecham Plc rose 1-1/4 to 89-1/4.

Venezuelan telephone company CANTV rose 1-11/16 in heavy trade to 42, above a 12-month closing high. Traders said the ADRs were acting as a proxy for the Venezuelan economy, with investors optimistic about prospects for privatization, signs of economic strength and positive comments about the country's power sector.
"This has nothing to do with the underlying fundamentals of the stock," a trader said.
Japan's Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd was up 5/8 to 20 after it said it planned to cut its risk-weighted assets by one trillion to three trillion yen in an effort to raise its capital adequacy ratio.
Advancers led decliners 226 to 178 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.33 percent and volume in mid-morning was 16 million ADRs.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
